description: Simple direct way to buy a digital gift card (Amazon, Steam, Apple, Netflix, Google Play, PlayStation, Xbox, IKEA, Airbnb, …) via natural language. Describe what you want in `prompt`, e.g. "steam 25 USD" or "amazon 50 euro germany". If country is omitted, US is used as default. Minimal card nominal is $1. The product and denomination are matched automatically: the closest package for the requested value is selected. Note: the card nominal is not the final charge - expect a deviation. The exact amount is shown in the 402 `accepts` - compare it against your request before signing. Flow: first call WITHOUT a payment signature returns isError=true with `x402Version` + `accepts` in structuredContent (the price is computed dynamically from the product and denomination you asked for). Sign those accepts and retry with `_meta["x402/payment"]` (base64 payload). On success returns the redemption code(s) under `structuredContent.redemption`, or `structuredContent.delivery="pending"` if not delivered yet - codes then appear later in `get_my_history` routes["gift-cards"].events[].params.redemption[].code If the product cannot be resolved or fails after you paid, the call is refunded automatically (structuredContent.refunded=true). Limits: 12 free probes/h per IP, then paid calls 300/5min per IP.

prompt.description: Natural-language purchase intent. Include brand, denomination, and optionally country.

name: buy_gift_cards

meta.description: Response metadata. Present in both success and error responses.

yourID.description: 8-char lowercase hex buyer ID assigned to the payer. Use it as `buyerID` in `get_my_history` to retrieve redemption codes once `delivery` becomes "delivered". Only present on success responses where the payer was identified; absent on pre-payment errors (400) and on refunded failures where the payer could not be resolved.
